adjudication_label: batch_1:APT field evaporation and voltage mode parameters
canonical_question: Why was the APT examination performed in voltage mode at 50 K instead of laser mode, and does this affect the spatial resolution of the δ-lamella interfaces?

question_variants.question: Why was the APT examination performed in voltage mode at 50 K instead of laser mode, and does this affect the spatial resolution of the δ-lamella interfaces?
question_variants.resolution_summary: The text confirms that APT was performed in voltage mode at 50 K but does not provide a comparative analysis with laser mode or discuss the impact of this choice on the spatial resolution of δ-lamella interfaces.

answers.answer: The document states that samples were examined at 50 K in voltage mode. It does not explain why laser mode was not used nor provide data on the spatial resolution effects on δ-lamella interfaces compared to laser mode.
answers.boundary_limitation: No comparison to laser mode or resolution metrics provided
evidence_spans: Bulk (W 1.5 Ni 2.25 Fe) 95 Ta 5 (W30-Ni45-Fe20-Ta5, in at.%) alloy ingots were prepared by arc melting pure metals (all with purity >99.99%) in an argon atmosphere.
Alloy samples were repeatedly melted at least 10 times to ensure uniform melting and improve their chemical homogeneity.

After cooling, the bulk ingots with dimensions of 50 mm × 50 mm × 10 mm were homogenized at 1200 °C for 5 h in an Ar atmosphere and subsequently hot-rolled at 1200 °C with a rolling reduction ratio of 80%, i.e., with a thickness reduction from 10 to 2 mm.

source_evidence_spans: These APT samples were examined at 50 K in voltage mode.
